debens.definition: (dēbēns ntis), m P. of debeo, a debtor ; only plur: fides debentium, L.

decem1.definition: decem (often written X), num: minae, ten, T.: hominum milia, Cs.: anni: decem novem, Cs.: decem et octo, Cs.: de tribus et decem fundis: decem primi, the presidents of a colonial senate.— As a round number: vitia, i. …

decem2.definition: decem prīmī ōrum, m the heads of the ten decuriae forming the senate in a colony or municipal town.

decens.definition: decēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of decet, seemly, becoming, decent, proper, fit : amictus, O.: motus, H.: quid verum atque decens, H.: (habitus) decentior quam sublimior, Ta.— Symmetrical, well-formed, beautiful, nob…

deceo.definition: (deceō cuī), —, —, ēre (only 3d pers.) DEC-, to be seemly, be comely, become, beseem, behoove, be fitting, be suitable, be proper : dubitabant quid deceret: quid deceat et quid aptum sit personis: nec scit quod augure…

decessus.definition: dēcessus ūs, m decedo, a going away, departure : Dionysii, N.— A withdrawal, retirement (from office): Bruti.— A subsidence, ebbing : aestūs, Cs.— Decease, death : amicorum.

decido1.definition: dēcidō cidī, —, ere de + cado, to fall down, fall off, fall away : anguis decidit de tegulis, T.: poma ex arboribus: e flore guttae, O.: ex equis, N.: equo, Cs.: in terras sidus, O.: in puteum auceps, H.: in turbam pr…

decido2.definition: dēcīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere de + caedo, to cut off, cut away : virgam arbori, Ta.: Te decisa dextera quaerit, V.— Prov.: pennas, to clip , H.—Fig., to decide, determine, settle, terminate, put an end to : sine me: pro se:…

deciens.definition: deciēns or deciēs num adv. decem, ten times : HS deciens centena milia: deciens centena dedisses Huic parco (sc. HS), H.—Ellipt. (sc. centena milia), a million : HS deciens et octingenta milia, i. e. 1,800,000 sesterc…

decimum.definition: decimum adv. decimus, for the tenth time , L.

decocta.definition: decocta ae, f decoctus; sc. aqua, water boiled down, a cold drink , Iu.

decoctus.definition: dēcoctus adj. P. of decoquo, ripe, mellow : suavitas (oratoris).

decolor.definition: dē-color ōris, adj., deprived of color, discolored, faded: sanguis: Indus, swarthy, O., Pr.: heres, colored, dark, Iu.: decolor fuligine, Iu.: sanguine, stained, O.—Fig., degenerate, depraved: aetas, V.: fama, O.

decore.definition: decōrē adv. decorus, suitably, properly, becomingly, decorously : ea facere: res p. gesta, S.: formata species, worthily .

decorum.definition: decōrum ī, n decorus, seemliness, propriety .

decretum.definition: dēcrētum ī, n decerno, a decree, decision, ordinance, vote, resolution : Hoc decreto eum consul senatu prohibuit, in pursuance of , Cs.: decreta vendere: recito decretum: decurionum: decretum fit, uti, etc., S. — A re…

decuma.definition: decuma or decima ae, f decimus; sc. pars, a tenth part, tithe, land-tax : hordei: Sardiniae binae decumae frumentae imperatae, L.: alquid sibi decumae dare: decumas vendere: prandia decumae nomine, i. e. a feast under…

decumanus.definition: decumānus or decimānus adj. decimus, of the tenth part, of tithes : ager, that pays tithes : frumentum, a tithe of the produce. — Collecting tithes, farming tithes : mulier, a tithe-farmer's wife .—As subst m., a tith…

decumates.definition: decumātes ium, adj. decimus, subject to tithes, tributary : agri, Ta.

decuriatus.definition: decuriātus ūs, m decurio, a dividing into decuriae : ad decuriatum convenire, L.

decurio2.definition: decuriō ōnis, m decuria, the chief of a decuria, commander of a decuria of cavalry , Cs.— A member of a municipal senate : decurionum decretum, Cs.

decursus2.definition: dēcursus ūs, m decurro, a running down, downward course, descent : aquarum, O.: rapidus (amnium), V.— A descent, attack : subitus ex collibus, L.: in litora, Ta.— An evolution, manœuvre : iustus, L.: legionum, Ta.— A …

decurtatus.definition: dē-curtātus adj., cut off, curtailed, mutilated. — Of style: quaedam decurtata.

dedeceo.definition: (dē-deceō) cuī, —, ēre, to be unseemly, misbecome, disfigure, disgrace (only 3d pers.; mostly impers.): ut, si quid dedeceat, vitemus: neque te Dedecet myrtus, H.: preces, quorum me dedecet usus, O.: Oratorem simulare…

dedecorus.definition: dē-decōrus adj., dishonoring, disgraceful: maioribus suis, Ta.

dedignor.definition: dē-dīgnor ātus, ārī, dep., to reject as unworthy, disdain, scorn, refuse: alquos maritos, V.: virum, O.: genibus procumbere Iovis, O.: venire, Ta.: sollicitare, O.

deditus.definition: dēditus adj. P. of dedo, given up, surrendered : senatum paenituit dediti principis.—Plur m . as subst, prisoners of war, captives : incolumitatem deditis polliceri, Cs.: adroganter in deditos consulere, Ta.—Fig., giv…

deductus.definition: dēductus adj. P. of deduco, lowered, unambitious, modest (poet.): carmen, V.: vox, Pr.

defectus1.definition: dēfectus adj. P. of deficio, weak, worn out, enfeebled : defecto poplite labens, O.: corpus, Ta.: amor, O.: annis, Ph.

defectus2.definition: dēfectus ūs, m deficio, a falling away, desertion, revolt : Spartanorum, Cu. — A diminution, failure : aquarum, L. — An obscuration, eclipse : solis, V.—Plur: eius (lunae).

defessus.definition: dēfessus adj. P. of defetiscor, worn out, weary, exhausted : verberando, T.: diuturnitate pugnae, Cs.: volneribus: bello, S.: cum integri defessis succederent, Cs.: Aeneadae, V.: accusatio, effete .

definitus.definition: dēfīnītus adj. P. of definio, limited, precise, definite : quaestionum (genus): locus.

deformo1.definition: dē-fōrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to bring into shape, form, depict, describe: quem supra deformavi.

defrutum.definition: dēfrutum ī, n de + FVR-, must boiled down , V.

degeneratum.definition: dēgenerātum ī, n P. of degenero, baseness, degeneracy : in aliis, L.

deiectio.definition: dēiectiō ōnis, f deicio.—In law, an ejection, dispossession : deiectionem facere.

deiectus2.definition: dēiectus ūs, m deicio, a throwing down, felling, fall : arborum, L.: gravis undarum, O.— A declivity, descent : collis, Cs.—Plur: collis deiectūs habebat, Cs.

despectus1.definition: dēspectus adj. with sup. P. of despicio, contemptible, scorned : maxime natura eius, Ta.: despectissima pars servientium, Ta.

desperanter.definition: dēspēranter adv. despero, hopelessly, despairingly : loqui secum.

desperatus.definition: dēspērātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of despero, given up, despaired of, irremediable, desperate : res p.: desperatas pecunias exigere: fuga.—Prov.: desperatis adhibere medicinam: haec nunc multo desperatiora: despe…

despiciendus.definition: dēspiciendus adj. P. of despicio, contemptible , Ta.

despiciens.definition: dēspiciēns entis, adj. P. of despicio, contemptuous : tam sui, of so little self-esteem .

destinatus.definition: dēstinātus adj. P. of destino, fixed, determined, destined, inevitable : sententiae: hora mortis: Orci finis, H.: destinatus obdura, resolutely , Ct.

desubito.definition: dē-subitō or dē subitō adv., on a sudden, suddenly: bolus ereptus e faucibus, T.: funus ornatum.

desuefactus.definition: dēsuēfactus adj. desuetus + factus, estranged : multitudo a contionibus.

detestandus.definition: detestandus adj. P. of detestor, execrable : fraus, Ta.

digne.definition: dīgnē adv. with comp. dignus, worthily, fitly, becomingly : laudari satis digne: iniuriam persequi: Martem scribere, H.: Peccare cruce dignius, H.

dignor.definition: dīgnor ātus, ārī, dep. dignus, to deem worthy, honor, deign, condescend : tali me honore, V.: quaecumque (loca) adventu, Ta.: alio te funere, V.: Bis septem ordinibus quam (summam) lex dignatur Othonis, requires for a…

digressus2.definition: dīgressus ūs, m digredior, a parting, separating, departure : meus: amici, Iu.

dii.definition: diī. 1. Nom. plur. of deus.— 2. Gen. of dies.

diiudicatio.definition: dīiūdicātiō ōnis, f diiudico, a judging, deciding .

diiudico.definition: dī-iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre, to distinguish, know apart, discern, perceive the difference: vera et falsa: vera a falsis: inter has sententias. — To judge, discern, decide, determine: dicam, quod mihi in mentemst, tu diiu…

dilator.definition: dīlātor ōris, m dis- + TAL-, a delayer, dilatory person , H.

dilectus1.definition: dīlēctus adj. P. of diligo, loved, beloved, dear : Maecenas, H.: Superis, O.: sorori, V.

dilectus2.definition: dīlēctus or dēlēctus ū s, m dis- or dē + 1 LEG-, a choosing, picking out, selecting, selection, choice, distinction : ad quod delectus adhibetur: iudicum: dignitatis: non dilectu aliquo ducitur ad iudicandum: sine ull…

diligenter.definition: dīligenter adv. with comp. and sup. diligens, industriously, attentively, diligently, assiduously : iter facere, Cs.: omnia agere: percipite quae dicam: diligentius (libelli) sunt reconditi: quos diligentissime conser…

dilucide.definition: dīlūcidē adv. dilucidus, plainly, evidently, distinctly : expedire Iudicibus, T.: explicare: respondeo.

dilutus.definition: dīlūtus adj. P. of diluo, thin, weak, dilute .— Comp.: dilutius poturi (sc. vinum).

diluvies.definition: dīluviēs —, acc. em, f diluo, an inundation, flood, deluge : fera, H.

dimano.definition: dī-mānō āvī, —, āre, to spread abroad: ad existimationem hominum latius.

dimetor.definition: dī-mētor (dē-) ātus, ārī, dep. and pass. —Dep., to measure out, mark out: eorum cursū s dimetati cognovimus.—Pass, to be measured out, be marked: locum castris dimetari iussit, L.: dimetata signa (al. demetata).

dimidiatus.definition: dīmidiātus adj. dimidium, halved, divided in the middle : mensis: partes versiculorum.

dimissus2.definition: (dīmissus ūs), m a deliverance. — Only dat: hanc quaestionem dimissui sperant futuram (dub.).

dimminuo.definition: dimminuō —, —, ere dis- + minuo, to break to pieces, shatter, break : tibi caput, T.: Dimminuetur tibi cerebrum, T.

dinosco.definition: dī-nōscō —, —, ere, to know apart, distinguish, discern: vera bona, Iu.: (geminos) inter se similes, O.: civem hoste, H.: dominum et servum deliciis, Ta.: curvo rectum, H.

dioecetes.definition: dioecētēs ae, m , dioikhth/s, an overseer of the revenue, royal treasurer.

dira1.definition: (dīra ae), f dirus, a bad omen (only plur.): dirae, sicut cetera auspicia, etc.— A curse, execration : Diris agam vos, H.: compositae, Ta.

directe.definition: dīrēctē adv. with comp. dirigo, in a straight line, precisely, exactly : ad perpendiculum, Cs.: directius gubernare: dicere.

diremptus2.definition: dīrēmptus ūs, m dirimo, a separation .

diribeo.definition: diribeō —, itus, ēre dis- + habeo, to separate, sort, canvass (ballots): dum de te tabellae diribeantur: diribitae tabellae.

dirigo1.definition: dīrigō rēxī, rēctus, ere dis- + rego, to distribute, scatter : volnera (i. e. tela), V.— To lay out, arrange in lines : regiones urbis: vicos, i. e. the rows of houses , L.

dis1.definition: dīs dītis, neut. dīte, adj. with comp. dītior and sup. dītissimus DIV-, rich, wealthy, opulent, provided, abounding : dis quidem esses, T.: Cratini huius ditis aedes, T.: domus, H.: patre diti, N.: Mycenae, H.: delubr…

discessus2.definition: discessus ūs, m dis- + 1 CAD-, a going asunder, parting : non longinquus inter nos: caeli, i. e. lightning.—A going away, departure, removal , withdrawal : tuus:. ab urbe: e vitā: latronis: meus, banishment : discessu…

discinctus.definition: discinctus adj. P. of discingo, ungirt, without the girdle : discincti ludere, in loose dress , i. e. at ease , H.— Voluptuous, effeminate, dissolute : Afri, V.: nepos, H.

discrepatio.definition: discrepātiō ōnis, f discrepo, a disagreement, dispute : inter consules, L.

discursus2.definition: discursus ūs, m discurro, a running to and fro, running about, straggling : continere ab discursu militem, L.: vallem discursibus impleat, O.: subito discursu, a double flank movement , Ta.

diserte.definition: disertē adv. with sup. disertus, clearly, eloquently, expressly : hoc scribere: disertissime scriptum, L.

disertus.definition: disertus adj. with comp. and sup. for * dissertus; P. of dissero, skilful, clear, clever, wellspoken, fluent : homo, T.: disertos cognosse me nonnullos: adulescens: ad vinum: calices quem non fecere disertum? H.: laud…

disiuncte.definition: (disiūnctē) adv. disiūnctus, separately, without connection .—Only comp: disiunctius dici.

disiunctio.definition: disiūnctiō or dīiūnctiō ōnis, f disiungo, a separation : meorum.— A variation, deviation : animorum: sententiae.— A logical opposition .— In rhet., asyndeton, a succession of clauses without connectives .

disiunctus.definition: disiūnctus (dīiūnc-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of disiungo, parted, separate, distant, remote : disiunctissimae terrae: Aetolia procul a barbaris disiuncta gentibus.—Fig., apart, different, remote, disconnected, str…

disiungo.definition: dis-iungō or dīiungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere, to unyoke: iumenta: bos disiunctus, H.: fessos iuvencos, O. — To disunite, sever, divide, separate, part, remove: (fons) munitione diiunctus a mari: Iugurthae Bocchique regnum (…

disor.definition: dis- or dī- praep., inseparable DVA-, disbefore c, p, q, s, t , dī- before d, g, l, m, n, r , and v (but usu. dimminuō, sometimes disrumpo), dif- before f Before a vowel dis- becomes dir-; before i consonant, sometime…

dispalatus.definition: dis-pālātus adj., straggling, astray: in agris, N.: multitudo, N.

dispar.definition: dis-pār aris, adj., unlike, dissimilar, different, unequal, ill-matched: dispares mores disparia studia sequentur: pari gratiā sed genere dispari, Cs.: certabant, ipsi pares, ceterum opibus disparibus, S.: rebus et or…

disparatum.definition: disparātum ī, n disparo.—In rhet., a direct opposition .

disperse.definition: dīspersē adv. dispersus, here and there, occasionally : dictae res: multis in locis dicta.

dispertio.definition: dispertiō īvī, ītus, īre dis- + partio, to distribute, divide : inter manipulos funditores, S.: pecuniam iudicibus: exercitum per oppida, L.: mensam servis, N.: portas tribunis, assign , S.— Fig., to divide, apportion…

displodo.definition: (dis-plōdō) —, ōsus, ere, to burst, cause to explode.—Only p. perf.: displosa vesica, H.

disposite.definition: dispositē adv. dispositus, orderly, methodically : accusare istum.

dispositus2.definition: (dispositus ūs), m a disposition, arrangement.—Only abl sing.: civilium rerum, Ta.

dissensus2.definition: (dissēnsus ūs), m dissentio, dissension, disagreement .—Only abl sing. : vario, V.

disserenasco.definition: (disserēnāscō) āvī, —, āre, inch impers. dis + sereno, to clear up, grow clear : cum undique disserenasset, L.

dissero1.definition: dis-serō —, —, ere, to plant here and there: taleae intermissis spatiis disserebantur, Cs.

dissero2.definition: dis-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to examine, argue, discuss, speak, harangue, discourse, treat: mecum: pluribus verbis sit disserendum: philosophiae pars, quae est disserendi: de omnibus rebus in contrarias partīs: pro legibu…

dissideo.definition: dissideō ēdī, —, ēre dis- + sedeo, to sit apart, be remote : sceptris quae (terra) libera nostris Dissidet, V.: quantum Hypanis dissidet Eridano, Pr. — Fig., to be at variance, disagree, differ : non consiliis, sed ar…

dissignatio.definition: dissīgnātiō ōnis, f dissigno, an arrangement (v. l. for designatio).

dissignator.definition: dissīgnātor (not dēsīg-), ōris, m dissigno, an undertaker, manager (at a funeral), H.

dissigno.definition: dis-sīgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to unseal, disclose: Quid non ebrietas dissignat? H. — Fig., to arrange, dispose, regulate, set in order (only v. l. for designo).

dissilio.definition: dissiliō uī, —, īre dis- + salio, to leap asunder, fly apart, burst, break up, split : mucro ictu dissiluit, V.: aera (sc. frigore), V.: Haec loca convolsa ruinā Dissiluisse ferunt, V.: Caput dissilire neniā, H.—Fig.,…

dissimiliter.definition: dissimiliter adv. dissimilis, differently, in a different manner : efficere voluptates: oppidum situm, S.: haud dissimiliter navibus vagis, L.

dissimulantia.definition: dissimulantia ae, f dissimulo, a dissembling .

dissipabilis.definition: dissipābilis e, adj. dissipo, that may be dispersed : ignis et aër.

dissipatus.definition: dissipātus adj. P. of dissipo, scattering, incoherent : oratio: dissipata conectere: in instruendo (orator).

dissipo.definition: dissipō or dissupō āvī, ātus, āre dis + * supo, throw, to spread abroad, scatter, disperse : ignis se dissipavit, L.: fratris membra: dissipatos homines congregare: venenum per ossa, O.: in mille curias dissipata res …

dissolute.definition: dissolūtē adv. with comp. dissolutus, loosely, disconnectedly : dicere. — Fig., laxly, negligently, carelessly : decumas vendere: alqd factum.

dissolutus.definition: dissolūtus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of dissolvo. — Of discourse, disjointed, loose, disconnected , C.—In rhet., as subst n., asyndeton , C.— Fig., of character, lax, remiss, negligent, careless, dissolute, abandone…

dissors.definition: dis-sors rtis, adj., of a different fate, not in common: ab omni milite gloria, O.

distaedet.definition: dis-tāedet —, —, ēre, impers, it is wearisome, is disgusting: cum hoc distaedet loqui, T.

distans.definition: dīstāns ntis, adj. P. of disto.—In space, remote, far apart, far away, distant : tam distantibus in locis: spatio distante, O.: legio mille passuum intervallo, at a distance , L.: loco ripae, O.: trabes inter se binos…

distentus1.definition: distentus adj. with comp. P. of distendo, distended, full : lacte capellae, V.: distentius uber, H.

distentus2.definition: distentus adj. with sup. P. of distineo, engaged, busied, occupied : negotiis: distentissimus de Buthrotiis: mens.

distincte.definition: dīstinctē adv. distinctus, with precision, distinctly, clearly : dicere: concisa brevitas.

distinctus1.definition: dīstinctus adj. with comp. P. of distinguo, separated, separate, distinct : genera delictorum: acies distinctior, ex pluribus partibus constans, L.: concentus ex distinctis sonis. — Decorated, adorned, studded, impres…

distinctus2.definition: (dīstinctus ūs), m STIG-. — Only abl. sing., variety : pinnarum, Ta.

distortus.definition: distortus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of distorqueo, distorted, misshapen, deformed, dwarfish : eiectā linguā: crura, H.: si distortissimi (sapientes) sint. — Fig.: nullum (genus enuntiandi) distortius, more perverse .

distribute.definition: distribūte adv. with comp. distributus, orderly, methodically : scribere: distributius tractare.

districtus.definition: dīstrictus adj. with comp. P of distringo, drawn in opposite ways, hesitating : districtus esse, quod, etc. — Harassed, distracted, busy : iudicio: ancipiti contentione: labore vita: omni Sollicitudine, H.: a causis d…

ditior.definition: dītior, dītissimus comp. and sup. of 1 dis.

diutius.definition: diūtius, diūtissimē comp. and sup. of diu.

diverse.definition: dīversē or dīvorsē adv. with comp, in different directions, different ways, hither and thither: divorsius concidere, S.: discedere, N. — Fig.: animum trahere, T.: de eādem re dici, variously.

diversor.definition: dīversor or dēversor ōris, m deverto, a guest : caupo cum quibusdam diversoribus.

diversus.definition: dīversus or dīvorsus adj. with sup. P. of diverto; dis + verto, turned different ways, opposite, contrary : in diversum iter equi concitati, L.: iter a proposito, Cs.: diversam aciem in duas partīs constituit, with a …

divine.definition: dīvīnē adv. with comp. divinus, by divine inspiration, prophetically : plura praesensa. — Admirably, divinely .

divisus2.definition: (dīvīsus, ūs) m divido, a division, distribution . — Only dat sing. : bona divisui fuere, L.: divisui facilis Macedonia, easily divided , L.

divolgatus.definition: dīvolgātus (dīvulg-) adj. with sup. P. of divolgo, widespread, common : divulgata veris ante habere, Ta.: magistratus divolgatissimus, made common .

divolgo.definition: dī-volgō or dī-vulgō āvī , ātus, āre, to spread among the people, make common, publish, betray, divulge: librum: consilium Domiti, Cs.: res gestas quo modo actae forent, S.: de te iam esse perfectum. — To make common,…

divum.definition: (dīvum ī), n 1 divus, the sky . — In phrases with sub : sub divo, under the sky, in open air : sub divo carpere somnos, V.: mori, H.: Sub divum rapere, expose, lay bare , H.

divus1.definition: dīvus ī, adj. DIV-, of a deity ; hence, godlike, divine : Iulius, deified . creatrix, V.

divus2.definition: dīvus ī (gen plur. dīvōm or dī vūm; rarely dīvōrum), m 1 divus, a god, deity, divine being : is divus (i. e. Apollo), L.: Dive, quem, etc., H.: Mortalin' decuit violari volnere divum? V.: boni divi, H.: praesentī s co…

docte.definition: (doctē) adv. doctus, only comp. and sup, learnedly, cleverly, skilfully : luctamur doctius, H.: litteris doctissume eruditus, S.

doctus.definition: doctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of doceo, learned, skilled, versed, experienced, trained, clever : vir: adulescentes doctissimi: abs te abire doctior, T.: ex disciplinā Stoicorum: mulier litteris, S.: fandi doctiss…

dolens.definition: dolēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of doleo, causing pain, distressing : alia (dicere) illis dolentia, S.: nil dolentius, O.— Afflicted : lenire dolentem, to comfort the sufferer , V.: dolentem Delenit usus, H.: dolente…

dolo1.definition: dolō āvī, ātus, āre DAL-, to chip with an axe, hew : robur: stipes falce dolatus, Pr.: robore dolatus. — To cudgel, belabor, drub : fuste, H. — Fig., to rough-hew, hack out : opus.

dolo2.definition: dolō or dolōn ōnis, m , do/lwn, an ironpointed staff, pike, sword-stick: saevi, V.—A sting, Ph.—The fore-topsail, L.

dominans.definition: domināns antis, adj. P. of dominor, ruling, bearing sway ; hence, nomina, used in a literal sense , H.—As subst m., a ruler : cum dominante sermones, Ta.: avaritia dominantium, Ta.

dominatus.definition: dominātus ūs, m dominor, rule, command, sovereignty, mastery, tyranny : regius: fit in dominatu servitus: in superbissimo dominatu esse: legiones ad suum dominatum convertere, Cs.— Fig., mastery, control : permittis i…

domino.definition: (dominō) —, —, āre dominus, to rule ; only pass: domus quam dispari Dominare domino! Poët. ap. C.

domitus2.definition: (domitus, ūs) m domo, a taming ; only abl sing. : quadrupedum.

donicum.definition: dōnicum conj, until, till: bellum persequi, donicum vicissent, N.

dotatus.definition: dōtātus adj. with sup. P. of doto, well endowed, gifted, provided : Aquilia: coniunx, H.: Chione dotatissima formā, O.

drachma.definition: drachma or dragma (old drachuma), ae, f , draxmh/, a drachma, drachm (a Greek coin, worth $0.19 or 9 1/2d.), T., C., H.

dubie.definition: dubiē adv., doubtfully, uncertainly dubius: signum datum: gaudere, O.—Usu. with a negative (haud, less frequently non or nec), without doubt, certainly, unquestionably : non dubie nuntiabatur, etc.: nec dubie ludibrio…

dubitans.definition: dubitāns adj. P. of dubito, wavering, irresolute.— Plur. m . as subst: dubitantes cogit, Cs.

ducentesimus.definition: ducentēsimus adj. ducenti, the two hundredth : lapis, Ta.: annus, Ta.—As subst f . (sc. pars), one two hundredth, a half per cent . (as a tax), Ta.

ducentiens.definition: ducentiēns (-iēs) adv. num. ducenti, two hundred times , C.—Poet., many times , Ct.

ductus2.definition: ductus ūs, m DVC-, a leading, conducting : aquae: aquarum: muri: oris, lineaments.— Military lead, conduct, generalship, command : rem ductu suo gerere: se ad ductum Pompei applicare.

dulce.definition: dulce adv. with comp. and sup. dulcis, agreeably, charmingly, delightfully : ridens, H., Ct.: dulcius canere, Pr.: historia scripta dulcissume.

dulciter.definition: dulciter adv. dulcis, agreeably, sweetly, pleasantly : sensus movetur.

dum1.definition: dum adv. of time, the while, a while, now, yet .—Only as enclitic; see etiamdum, nondum, nihildum, etc.—With imper. (colloq.): Sosia Adesdum, paucis te volo, stop a moment, T.: abidum, T.: facitodum, T.: age dum, T.: …

dumeta.definition: dūmēta (dumm-) ōrum, n dumus, thorn bushes, a thorn-hedge, thicket : saeptum dumetis sepulchrum: tondere dumeta, V.—Fig., intricacy, obscurity : Stoicorum: in dumeta conrepere.

dummodo.definition: dummodo or dum modo see 2 dum.

duo2.definition: duo virī, duovirī or II virī (less correctly duūmvirī) ōrum, m a board of two persons, an extraordinary criminal court, duumviri (selected by Tullus Hostilius to try Horatius), L.; (by the people to try Manlius), L.; …

duodeciens.definition: duodeciēns (-iēs) adv. num. cf. duodecim, twelve times .

duodeni.definition: duodēnī ae, a, adj. num distr. cf. duodecim, twelve each, twelve apiece : uxores habent deni inter se communīs, Cs.: in singulos homines iugera: Per duodena astra, twelve each year , V.: signa, O.

duodetriciens.definition: duo-dē-trīciēns adv. num, twenty-eight times, HS (sc. centena milia).

duodetriginta.definition: duo-dē-trīgintā or duo dē xxx adj. num, twenty-eight: castella, L.

duodeviceni.definition: duo-dē-vīcēnī ae, a, adj. num distr., eighteen each: denarii, L.

duoetvicesimani.definition: duo-et-vīcēsimānī ōrum, m soldiers of the twenty-second legion, Ta.

duoviratus.definition: (duovirātus or) II virātus acc., um duoviri, the office of a duumvir : II viratum gerere.

duplus.definition: duplus adj. DVA- + PLE-, double, twice as large, twice as much : intervalla: pecunia, L.—As subst n., the double, twice as much : dupli poena: in duplum ire, have a (new) trial for twice the amount .

dure.definition: dūrē adv. with comp. durus, hardly, stiffly, awkwardly : pleraque Dicere, H.: durius incedit, O.: quid fusum durius esset, H.— Harshly, roughly, sternly, rigorously : dicere: suae vitae durius consulere, i. e. kill th…

duriter.definition: dūriter adv. durus, roughly, coarsely : vitam agere, T.— Fig., harshly, sternly : Factum, T.
